questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a labelled diagram of the electrolytic cell used. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*What to draw:*

- A beaker (the electrolytic cell) containing **aqueous copper (II) sulphate** (the electrolyte, blue solution).
- Two **graphite rods** dipping into the solution: the **anode** (+) connected to the positive terminal and the **cathode** (-) connected to the negative terminal of a **d.c. supply (battery)**.
- Connecting wires from the electrodes to the battery, with a switch (and, if wanted, an ammeter or bulb) in the circuit.

Label: electrolyte (copper (II) sulphate solution), anode (+), cathode (-), graphite electrodes, battery/d.c. source.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the products formed at each electrode: Cathode: ......... Anode: ......... *[2 marks]*

The graphite electrodes are replaced with copper electrodes.

(i) Write equations for the reactions taking place at each electrode: Cathode: ......... Anode: .........

(ii) State the difference in the observations at the anode when the inert electrodes are replaced by copper electrodes. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Cathode:** $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$ (copper is deposited).

**Anode:** $\mathrm{Cu} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2e^-$ (copper dissolves).

(ii) With **graphite (inert) anode**, bubbles of oxygen gas are given off and the anode is unchanged. With the **copper anode**, **no gas is evolved**; instead the anode **gets smaller (dissolves, loses mass)**, and the blue colour of the solution stays the same because the copper ions removed at the cathode are replaced by those formed at the anode.

questions.enonce_markdown: A current of 1.0 A is passed through a solution of copper (II) sulphate for 50 minutes. Calculate the quantity of electricity passed in coulombs. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Quantity of electricity $Q = I \times t$, with the time in seconds.

$t = 50 \times 60 = 3000\ \mathrm{s}$

$Q = 1.0 \times 3000 = \mathbf{3000\ C}$ (that is $3.0\times10^{3}$ coulombs).
